impacts: Built four role-scoped consoles (operator, funder, supplier, lessee) on Next.js 16, Prisma and Postgres, where every step is an anti-fraud gate re-derived on the server and each transition appears live to all actors.

Implemented deterministic pricing, credit, e-invoice, serial-number, residual-value, ESG and bank-account modules, covered by nine Vitest evaluation suites, plus a hash-chained audit ledger per leased asset.

Produced the viability report, the technical specification and a Phase-1 integrations study (32 sources, 75 adversarially verified claims) that maps build-vs-buy choices for payments, e-invoicing, KYC, AML and e-signatures.

title: Corridor Pick-Up Site Study: Mobility-Driven Market Sizing for a Consumer-Electronics Brand
description: Delivered an interactive location study for a global consumer-electronics brand's pick-up point on an industrial corridor in the Guadalajara metro area, sizing its addressable market across residential, pass-through and workforce demand.
impacts: Quantified three additive demand layers: 50,970 target households in a 20-minute drive catchment (~312K people), pass-through anchored to official SICT TDPA 2024 counts (122,683 unique people per month) and 21,432 DENUE-declared jobs within 2 km.
Calibrated the device panel's expansion factors by socioeconomic stratum, traced pass-through origins nationwide and measured the airport-bound origin–destination share instead of assuming it.
Iterated the report through nine versions (v1.0–v1.8), root-causing seven numeric bugs and replacing a biased composite score with comparisons on homologous axes.

title: Territory Growth System: AI-Assisted Distribution Planning for a Coatings Manufacturer
description: Built an AI-assisted territory-growth system for a Mexican paint and coatings manufacturer that crosses its commercial portfolio with territorial census data to decide which clients to convert, where to prospect and where to open flagship stores across 16 Monterrey-area municipalities.
impacts: Designed 10 decision modules on a shared MapLibre canvas covering competitive gaps, client-conversion priorities, 378 qualified prospects with weekly visit routes and 10 candidate flagship-store zones.
Built a dual-brain AI analyst (Claude tool-calling with a deterministic fallback router running the same tools), so every figure comes from code with a visible provenance class.
Froze the output of a byte-deterministic Python ETL as typed datasets with gated, explainable scoring, a machine-checked 10-scene guided tour and a 110-file Vitest suite.

title: Official Store-Locator Registry: Monthly Retail Footprint Scraping Framework
description: Built a monthly branch registry for Mexican retail chains that uses only official sources: it scrapes each brand's own store locator, normalizes locations to a single schema and diffs runs to detect openings and closings.
impacts: Engineered a declarative adapter framework with six extraction strategies (JSON APIs, embedded JSON, sitemap/JSON-LD, HTML listings, grid sweeps and real-browser XHR capture) and shipped 90 brand adapters that yielded 20,805 accepted branch locations in the September 2026 run.

Enforced a single-source rule: no aggregators or map APIs as location sources, and geocoding only for addresses the brand itself published. The rule is backed by QA gates, frozen fixtures and 206 pytest tests.

Handled anti-bot store locators conservatively, using a real, headed Chrome profile that stops at any CAPTCHA challenge and never solves or retries it. Exported results to Parquet and GeoJSON with a per-batch progress board across 406 registered brands.

title: State Geo-Intelligence Platform: Economic-Census Explorer with a RAG Agent
description: Prototyped a state-level geo-intelligence platform for a Mexican state's sustainable-development agency that puts environmental, industrial and public-program modules over a single economic-census map, with roles, an audit trail and an AI agent that cites its sources.
impacts: Implemented three operational modules across the state's 18 municipalities: environmental inspections with 16 category filters and offline field capture, industrial-park mapping with SME–industry matching, and a five-program beneficiary and coverage suite.
Built a RAG agent with source citation and guardrails that answers through Claude when configured and falls back to a local BM25 retriever, on web chat and WhatsApp.
Designed a data layer that switches between seed data and Supabase (PostGIS/pgvector with row-level security) and server-side filtering that sustained a 220,000-unit synthetic census.

title: Big-Box Site Study: Home-Improvement Retail Location Intelligence
description: Delivered a multi-format site study for a Latin American home-improvement retailer's prospective big-box store in the Monterrey metro area, combining ten documented models, from household spending baskets and pass-by mobility to origin–destination capture and cannibalization, in one auditable web report, deck and data package.
impacts: Built read-only Python models over census, NSE, ENIGH 2024 spending, DENUE on H3, device mobility and a 21M-row origin–destination matrix. Each model emits a summary the integrator only copies, so no figure is typed by hand.

Measured cannibalization against the chain's existing stores with a layered ladder (geometric overlap, O-D origin overlap, co-visits, drive-time convenience) and calibrated pass-by traffic with site-specific NSE scaling.
Shipped an interactive report with 16 GeoJSON layers, a 33-slide deck, a PDF, an XLSX and a data ZIP, gated by build-failing validators after a 47-fix expert review.

title: Vacation-Rental Intelligence: Lodging Market Platform for a State Government
description: Built a password-gated short-term-rental intelligence platform for a Mexican state government that maps 42,357 vacation-rental listings to show lodging-tax gaps, tourism performance, housing pressure and competition with formal hotels.
impacts: Delivered an editorial insights tab and a map explorer with lazy-loaded municipal clusters and H3 heat layers over 42,357 listings in 10+ municipalities.
Sized the lodging-tax visibility gap on unregistered listings and tracked occupancy, ADR, RevPAR and available days by destination against official hotel statistics.
Built a resumable, idempotent Python pipeline that unifies rental and hotel supply into one accommodation layer, packed to stay under 5 MB compressed.

title: Acceptance Radar: Merchant Payment-Acceptance Propensity Platform
description: Built a territorial payment-acceptance platform for a global payments network that scores Mexico's ~5.5M merchants with an explainable conversion-propensity model and lets teams filter, map and export prioritized merchants with coordinates.
impacts: Engineered a Node ETL that extracts 5.49M POIs with payment-method flags from a read-only 45 GB Postgres warehouse into DuckDB and publishes a 70 MB Parquet+zstd serving artifact.
Designed a geometric propensity core (transaction value × acceptance gap × viability × neighborhood pressure) with three-state payment evidence and completeness shrinkage below 0.35 confidence.
Cut a percentile step that hung for over 40 minutes to 12 seconds with exact mid-rank percentiles over distinct values, and made map, list and export counts always match.

title: Motorcycle Retail Area Study: Corridor Attractiveness & Bottom-Up Sales Projection
impact: Robustness: Winner Stable Under ±50% Weight Shifts
description: Delivered a bilingual area study for a motorcycle brand's new point of sale in a large State of Mexico municipality, ranking four commercial corridors with a seven-factor attractiveness index and projecting monthly unit sales bottom-up from official registration and census data.
impacts: Built a 30-script Python pipeline feeding a static MapLibre + ECharts report that reads every figure from JSON at runtime, with no hand-typed numbers.
Designed a seven-factor corridor index and stress-tested it by moving each weight ±50%; the top corridor stayed the same in every case.

Projected demand as a band by triangulating INEGI's definitive vehicle-registration series (+212,481 motorcycles in the State of Mexico in 2024) with census motorcycle ownership, and shipped Spanish and English editions on one data contract.

title: Expansion Intelligence OS: AI-Operated Retail Expansion Planning
description: Built an AI-operated expansion operating system, deployed as executive demos for two national retail chains and a global quick-service restaurant brand, that takes expansion teams from territorial analysis to site evaluation, deterministic monthly financials and a five-year opening plan.
impacts: Built a dual-brain AI analyst: Claude tool-calling over deterministic services with an intent-router fallback for when the live model is unavailable, driving the map through a typed visual-action bus (87% prompt-cache hit rate).
Engineered a deterministic monthly financial engine calibrated to public disclosures within +0.27% on published sales productivity, feeding site evaluation, scenarios and a five-year plan.

Integrated warehouse data through a read-only ETL (184 road-network isochrones, 19 DENUE editions, a 4,894-cell H3 demand layer) and adapted the financial engine from grocery retail to quick-service formats, with 235–286 automated tests per deployment.

title: Mall Brand-Fit Study: Fashion Retail Expansion Scorecard
description: Built a reproducible Node.js and PostgreSQL pipeline and a single-file editorial report that scored eight brands of a global fashion retail group for an opening at a major shopping mall in northwestern Mexico.
impacts: Wrote SQL verification gates that changed conclusions: an exact mall filter (165 units, 133 open, matching the operator's published count) and a block on peso-denominated market size once household-survey spend periodicity proved undeterminable.
Replaced Euclidean rings with Mapbox drive-time isochrones: the 15-minute isochrone holds 34% fewer households than a 7 km ring (81,827 vs. 124,838), so rings overstated the reachable market.
Rendered 13,358 block polygons on a Leaflet canvas with integer delta-encoded geometry, inside a deterministic build that reproduces the analysis and the report byte for byte.

title: Industrial Development Model: Excel-Parity Decision Studio
description: Rebuilt an industrial real-estate development Excel workbook as a TypeScript web app whose deterministic financial engine matches the source model cell by cell.
impacts: Built a pure TypeScript engine for land bank, construction, lease-up, vacancy and market share across 20 markets and 21 years (2027–2047), matching 420/420 market-projection cells and all 105 project columns within 1e-4 in a Vitest parity harness.

Completed the returns layer the workbook left blank (IRR, NPV, MOIC, yield-on-cost) and documented fixes for template bugs, such as an HLOOKUP keyed on calendar years that assigned year-21 costs to every project.

Added scenario comparison, sensitivity sweeps with tornado charts, live narrative summaries, input guardrails and URL-compressed sharing in a client-only SPA with zero production npm audit vulnerabilities.

title: Pulso del Centro: Downtown Monterrey Mobility Platform
description: Built an interactive Next.js platform that turned a colleague's location-data study of downtown Monterrey into explorable passer-by KPIs, origin maps and zone comparisons.
impacts: Implemented a radius dial from 100 to 1,000 m that recomputes KPIs, map and audience profile live, backed by a server-side KPI endpoint and URL-shareable state.
Compiled a typed dataset from the study's JSON and Parquet aggregates with a Python build step, using only k-anonymized outputs (at least 5 people per cell) derived from a 460M-ping device panel.
Integrated an AGEB-level socioeconomic correction and a robustness panel, unified population scaling across views and added a fail-closed password gate before deploying to Vercel.

title: GeoKG Lab: Governed Geospatial Knowledge Graph with Claude Tools
description: Researched and built a reproducible geospatial knowledge-graph demo that keeps the spatial database as the source of truth while serving a validated read-only snapshot to graph queries, an expansion lab and optional Claude tool use.
impacts: Built a read-only extraction path (allowlisted SELECT queries, read-only transactions and rollback) into a content-hashed snapshot of 16 municipalities and 128 H3 cells, described by an OWL vocabulary with SHACL constraints.

Implemented an Expansion Lab with Pareto shortlists, sensitivity checks and portfolio sequencing, plus multi-hop graph queries that return evidence chains with explicit caveats that adjacency is not a route.

Gated an optional Claude Haiku 4.5 conversation behind explicit opt-in, typed local tools, numeric grounding checks and per-turn and per-session cost caps, verified by 149 backend and 31 frontend tests.

title: LandOptima: Satellite Footprint Capture Tool for HBU Analysis
impact: Click Fallback: Open Buildings → OSM → Manual
description: Built a browser tool that captures building and lot footprints from satellite imagery by search or click, classifies them and exports one GeoJSON collection for a Tijuana highest-and-best-use dashboard.
impacts: Replaced vertex-by-vertex polygon drawing with a search-or-click loop that pulls Google outlines, ML-derived Google Open Buildings footprints or OpenStreetMap footprints, degrading gracefully to manual drawing.

Wrote a DuckDB extractor that downloads only a city bounding box from the public Open Buildings bucket (79,746 Tijuana footprints at confidence ≥ 0.75 and ≥ 150 m²) instead of the full 178 GB dataset.
Defined a GeoJSON contract with typed plaza metadata and a single axis-order conversion module, and served the Maps API key from a local server rather than embedding it in the HTML.

title: Laya Decision Studio: Local Multimodal Typed-Decision Workbench
description: Built a local FastAPI workbench for typed yes/no, choice and score decisions over text, images and video frames, with an evaluation harness that separates working software from model quality.
impacts: Served the Laya decision model and Qwen3-VL-2B vision locally with pinned model revisions, explicit device reporting and bounded image and timestamped-frame inputs, plus labeled evaluation that reports accuracy, Brier score, NLL and ECE.

Ran an independent 24-request Coding Lab benchmark in which Laya got more individual decisions right than a rules baseline (238/288 vs. 226/288) but fewer complete specifications (2/24 vs. 5/24), and reported that result as measured.
Connected the model to Codex through an MCP server and CLI with a versioned repair ledger, and kept it out of review filtering after a held-out diagnostic caught only 1 of 12 positive cases.

title: QSR Franchise Expansion: Interactive Site-Selection Report
description: Rebuilt a 29-page location-intelligence PDF as an interactive, password-protected web report that benchmarked two operating restaurants of a pizza franchisee against two prospective sites in southeastern Mexico.
impacts: Structured the report for 10-second, 2-minute and 10-minute reads, leading with a per-site verdict built on a nine-dimension location-DNA benchmark drawn from the existing stores.

Added Leaflet maps for visitor-origin heat, AGEB choropleths by neighborhood and origin-destination flows over 5, 8 and 10-minute drive-time isochrones and 400 and 800 m walking buffers from a 32-day mobility window.
Protected the static site with a Vercel Edge Middleware gate that signs an HMAC-SHA256 cookie token and compares it in constant time, plus CSP, HSTS and noindex headers.

title: mireporte.ai: Point-Based Market Study Generator
description: Led development of mireporte.ai, a BlackPrint product that turns a point on a map into a frozen 25-section market study with ten data layers, a printable PDF, a folio and hashes of its sources.
impacts: Expanded coverage from three to eleven metro areas with per-city data contracts that fail the build on count drift, sha256 manifests for every source file and declared coverage gates.
Compressed the spatial index so eleven cities fit Vercel's 250 MB function limit, going from about 400 MB uncompressed to 149 MB for the largest function.
Recorded design decisions in 19 ADRs and kept a 5,043-test Vitest suite across 179 files green, including frozen golden reports per city.

title: Cataract Care Expansion: Territorial Prioritization Platform
description: Built a territorial prioritization platform and reports for a Mexican social enterprise expanding affordable eye surgery, scoring states and municipalities on modeled demand and supply gaps.
impacts: Built a Next.js 16 platform whose MapLibre map clusters 11,405 georeferenced eye-care and health facilities from DENUE and CLUES, with an accessible SVG choropleth as fallback.

Designed an offline GeoPandas pipeline that measures distances in EPSG:6372 and assigns facilities to 2,469 municipalities through point-in-polygon joins, with Zod schemas validating the data at build time.
Tested ranking robustness with a Monte Carlo re-weighting analysis (P5–P95 rank ranges) and labeled every priority score in the interface as modeled, not measured.
